verdict.rationale: incident.io ships a first-party remote MCP server, so users can query incidents, analyze alerts, check on-call and manage escalations through natural-language AI assistants. A changelog entry also says the status page can now be updated 'using the agent', which points to some in-product natural-language control. However, the native agent's command surface is only thinly evidenced, and natural-language operation mostly depends on an external MCP-capable assistant. missing for 10: documented native natural-language command interface covering core actions (declaring/resolving incidents, editing schedules), detail on which write actions are supported via the agent or MCP, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Query incidents, analyze alerts, check who's on call, manage escalations, and run deep operational analysis — all from your existing AI tools.
The incident.io MCP server lets you connect any AI assistant that supports the Model Context Protocol directly to your incident data.
You can now update your status page using the agent
